Working Together for a Greener Community: Ennis West Men’s Shed and Cnoc Na Scoile Residents Group Unite!
Cnoc Na Scoile Residents group and the Ennis West Mens Shed are teaming up to boost communication and support biodiversity in their 
community. Their first project is the creation of a community notice board that will be installed in the estate, making it easier for everyone 
to stay informed. The notice board will be crafted by the talented members of the Shed in Cloughleigh. This collaboration has been made 
possible through the support of Clare County Council’s, Rural Development Directorate, which encourages communities to collaborate and 
create positive change together. 
 
Left to Right - Kieran Walsh, Finbar Pickett, Ennis West Mens Shed, Anna Newmann & Natasha McCormack, Cnoc Na Scoile Residents Group, 
Niamh Wiley, RCDO, Clare County Council, Sal Milan, Ennis West Mens Shed.
Extension to Drumcliff Burial Ground:
The Burial Grounds Unit are progressing plans to extend the county burial ground at Drumcliff, Ennis. The proposed development is designed 
to address the growing need for burial space and aims to enhance the existing burial ground while creating a tranquil and reflective 
environment. The plan includes an addition of 413 double plots, including provision for ash plots, to meet the increasing demand for burial 
space. Additionally, a future Columbarium Wall is proposed which can contain up to 470 niches. The proposed extension aims to create a 
modern lawn cemetery that responds to the needs of our community. The design is driven by principles of accessibility and looks to promote 
biodiversity through the provision of planting and trees. An application to extend Drumcliff Burial Ground was submitted to An Coimisiún 
Pleanála in September.

Healthy Clare/Creative Ireland Micro Fund 2025 
A number of Healthy Clare micro funded projects were completed 
during the month of September. 
•	
Clare Traveller Community Development Project: Gym 
Wellbeing Project. 
This programme is co-funded by Healthy Clare and Clare Local 
Development Company and takes place in Active Ennis facilities. 
The gym initiative is designed for 10 Traveller men, emphasising the 
importance of mental health, physical health, and social inclusion. 
The project commenced with the aim of fostering a supportive 
environment that promotes overall well-being through fitness and at 
a mid point review it was found that the gym programme for Traveller 
men is achieving its objectives by making strides in physical fitness, 
supporting mental health, and encouraging inclusion. ‘The initiative 
not only improved physical health metrics but also significantly 
contributed to the mental and emotional well-being of the 
participants. Continued support and expansion of such programmes 
are essential for sustaining these benefits and promoting a healthier 
more inclusive lifestyle in the Traveller community.’
•	
West Limerick Resources, Social Farming: 
Social Farming is the practice of offering activity on family farms as a 
form of Social Support service. In Social Farming the farm remains a 
working farm at its core but invites people to participate in the day 
to day activities on the farm.
Three participants were supported to engage in Social Farming 
activity with farms in Feakle and Inagh because of the Healthy 
Clare Micro Fund. The evaluation showed that ‘All participants are 
thoroughly enjoying their social farming placement and positively 
engaging in health enhancing activities.’
•	
Lisdoonvarna Failte Fitness Programme: Lisdoonvarna
Failte ran a series of fun, inclusive fitness programmes to support 
the community to develop an awareness of how to live well through 
movement and social engagement. Activity included Zumba classes 
and mindful movement. 
•	
Peer Led Wellness Café Walks: 
Supported under the Healthy Clare Micro Fund, Creative Ireland 
collaboration, The Peer Led Wellness Café has completed a series 
of wellbeing walks engaging local historian Dr Jane O’Brien. on the 
8th of September. Feedback from the walks has been very positive 
and the café hopes that social opportunities beyond the café can be 
explored over the coming months.

Age Friendly Universities 
On 2nd September 2025, the Clare Age Friendly Programme proudly 
participated in the Age Friendly University initiative meeting - a 
pivotal moment in Ireland’s journey toward inclusive education.
The University of Limerick is set to become the first institution in the 
country to adopt the World Health Organization’s four-stage process 
in pursuit of official recognition as an Age Friendly University. This 
structured approach includes commitment, assessment, planning, 
and implementation - all aimed at creating a welcoming, accessible, 
and enriching environment for learners of all ages.
This collaboration marks a transformative step forward in promoting 
lifelong learning, intergenerational engagement, and age-inclusive 
policies within higher education. Clare’s involvement underscores 
the region’s dedication to championing age-friendly values across 
communities and institutions.

Cultural Companions Event 
On September 4th, the Cultural Companion group came together 
for a lively and enriching day filled with creativity, movement, and 
local charm. The event kicked off with registration and a captivating 
walking tour of Ennis, where participants uncovered the town’s 
hidden stories and historical gems. Trish Cleary then guided 
attendees through gentle chair yoga sessions, offering a moment 
of calm and connection. Artistic inspiration continued with pottery 
demonstrations by Oak House Ceramics and candle-making insights 
from Gealach Candles. Adding a seasonal touch, Andrea O’Regan led 
a hands-on autumn wreath-making workshop, where participants 
crafted beautiful, nature-inspired decorations to celebrate the 
changing season. The day was a perfect blend of discovery, artistry, 
and community spirit.
North Clare Positive Aging & Wellness Fair 
The North Clare Positive Ageing and Wellness Event took place 
on Saturday, September 6th, and was met with an enthusiastic 
and high turnout from the local community. Designed to promote 
health, wellbeing, and active ageing, the event offered a full day of 
engaging presentations, physical activities, and opportunities for 
social connection. The day began with a warm welcome and opening 
remarks from Joe Killeen, setting a positive tone for the sessions 
ahead. Carmel Burke, the event coordinator, guided attendees 
through the day with care and attentiveness, offering both the initial 
health and safety briefing and closing thanks.
Throughout the event, participants enjoyed multiple exercise 
sessions led by Niall and Trish Cleary, which encouraged movement 
and physical engagement. Sharon Cahir of Cahir Solicitors in Ennis 
provided valuable legal insights tailored to older adults, followed by 
an interactive Q&A. Consultant Nutritionist Grainne Travers shared 
expert advice on healthy eating and lifestyle choices, while Sgt 
Cathriona Houlihan from the Clare Crime Prevention Unit and Ronan 
Buntung of Task Community Care addressed safety and support 
services available to the ageing population. Jenny O’Mara, Social 
Worker for the Older Person with Eimear Sutton Horan on the Clare 
Home and Day Care Services, concluded the speaker lineup with a 
thoughtful overview of care services and support networks in the 
region.
Overall, the event was a resounding success, reflecting the strength 
and vibrancy of the North Clare community. It fostered awareness, 
empowerment, and connection among older adults, and highlighted 
the value of collaboration in promoting wellness and ageing with 
dignity.
 
Healthy Ireland
Healthy Ireland Local Government hosted a national two-day 
conference - “Building Resilient Futures through Local Government" 
September 11th -12th 2025, in the SETU Arena, Waterford
The conference brought together leaders, planners, and officials 
across local government to explore how Ireland’s local authorities 
can lead and collaborate more effectively to address health 
inequalities and the wider determinants of wellbeing. With a strong 
focus on breaking down silos, creating joined-up opportunities, and 
harnessing evidence and place-based tools, the event aims to inspire 
transformative local action for healthier, more resilient communities. 
The objectives of the Conference was to
•	
Enable local government to act as strategic leaders in integrating 
policy for impact, 
•	
Promote integration across policy strands and Directorates 
•	
Build capacity for using tools for transformation like the Place 
Standard and Healthy Ireland Data Portal. 
•	
Encourage a move towards collaborative community resilience
Speakers included: 
Minister of State, Mary Butler TD who launched the Healthy Ireland 
Local Government Data Portal, Sean Mc Keown Chief Executive 
Waterford City & County Council, Maarten Nijpels (City of Rotterdam), 
Kristen Guidan (London Resilience), Dr Tony Holohan (WHO & UCD), 
John Howie (Public Health Scotland) and Roisin Markham (Irish 
Doughnut Economic Network)

Young library member attending the Books at Bedtime event in

September. Each child in Clare aged 3 and under was offered a 
free copy of the book 'Say Goodnight Like This' by Mary Murphy to

Healthy Ireland 
A walk-in health check was organized in collaboration with HSE 
nurses as part of the recent Pop-up literacy event in Kilkee Library. 
Attendees were offered complimentary blood pressure checks, 
diabetes screening, and general health advice. A total of 55 
individuals participated in the community health initiative. Shannon 
Library hosted a talk with Mental Health Ireland on the topic of ‘The 
Five Ways to Wellbeing.’ This talk offers practical steps to people to 
improve their mental health and lead a more balanced and fulfilling 
life.
Creative Ireland Programme
 The Clare Culture and Creativity Team, which includes representatives 
from the Library, Arts, Heritage, Local Enterprise Office, Climate 
Action, Biodiversity, Museum, Healthy Clare, Local Studies, and 
Rural Development sections of our Council, receive funding from 
Creative Ireland to support the development of cultural and creative 
initiatives throughout the county. This funding enables the team to 
strengthen community engagement and enhance creative capacity 
through a wide range of programmes and projects. Among the 
projects supported were the Cultural Companions Creative Event 
at Temple Gate Hotel, delivered by the Age Friendly Team, and 
the Heritage Office’s programme “Reading Your Local Landscape”, 
a course designed to explore Clare’s natural, built, and cultural 
heritage.
Creative Ireland also supported a multidisciplinary event titled 
“Lost in Briars”, which featured a panel discussion on the evolving 
relationship with the bramble - one of Ireland’s most common 
plants - and its ecological and cultural significance. The event 
included a Botanical Art Class facilitated by Jane Carkill and a live 
music performance by Simon O'Reilly, both of which focused on 
the bramble and its fruit, the blackberry. This event was held at the 
Courthouse Gallery in Ennistymon.
In addition, Creative Ireland funded the creative workshops for 
Music Generation’s Folk Festival. This inclusive festival promoted 
participation, education, and heritage, offering young musicians 
the opportunity to engage in collaborative learning and perform 
alongside professional artists.
Two Culture Night events also received support from Creative 
Ireland Clare. The first,” Seal le Ceri” in Scéal Eile Books, was an 
Irish language event where artist Ceri Garfield discussed her artistic 
practice and presented her work. The second featured North Clare 
Refugee Allstars, a unique musical collaboration with asylum seeker 
musicians living in IPAS centres across County Clare, who performed 
in Shannon in collaboration with Mná le Chéile Women’s Shed and 
developed in partnership with Clare Local Development Company 
and the Clare Immigrant Support Centre.
Local Studies and Archives 
Local Studies and Archives have received a donation of documents 
relating to the Vandeleur estate in Kilrush. These date from the 
1790s to the 1920s and contain a wealth of detail on the running of 
the estate. Thanks to the Noctor family of Limerick for the donation. 
A donation of books relating to the history of Clare was donated by 
the Collins family of Clare Road. This collection belonged to Michael 
Collins, a prominent local historian. A presentation was given to the 
Women’s PROBUS group, on the holdings in the Local Studies and 
Archives Centre. 
A collection of papers relating to the Creagh family of Dangan, Quin, 
was donated to Archives. The ongoing cataloguing of the Holohan 
Collection has uncovered an interesting find, a letter from the Clare 
MP William Redmond.

Clare Museum 
The Museum winter lecture series has been finalised with lectures 
taking place between October to May 2026. The temporary O’Connell 
Exhibition is on view at the museum. Four new items were added to 
the long-term exhibition, replacing items that have been on display 
since the museum opened. A blog on two of the items was written 
and placed on the museum website.
A further 27 objects were catalogued onto the Museum database, 
bringing the total for the year to 248. There were 46 new items 
photographed and uploaded to the museum website and there were 
five social media posts during the month.

Local Authority Integration Team
The Local Authority Integration Teams (LAITs) have been set up 
in all local authorities. Their purpose is to help coordinate the 
different kinds of support available for people who are applying 
for international protection, refugees, and others in similar 
situations. 
The goal of LAITs is to help IP applicants and refugees become 
independent, settle into their new communities, and participate 
in Irish life. They do this by connecting people to important 
LOCAL AUTHORITY INTEGRATION TEAM

services that can help them integrate into the community. 
Who do LAITs support? 
LAITs provide support for: 
•	 Applicants for International Protection (IP) 
•	 People who have been granted refugee status or other forms 
	
of protection, such as subsidiary protection or permission to 
	
remain 
•	 Refugees who have been resettled in Ireland through a 
	
government programme 
•	 Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection (BOTPs) 
 
How is the support provided? 
LAITs operate under the principle of 'Integration from Day One'. 
This means that LAITs provide integration support to people 
who need it as soon as they arrive in Ireland. 
What services do LAITs provide? 
The work of LAITs isn’t meant to replace existing services. 
Instead, LAITs help connect people with the existing services 
that are most suitable for their needs. This includes things like: 
•	 Being a direct contact for new arrivals, helping them with any 
	
problems they might have when dealing with public services 
•	 Connecting new arrivals with services like legal help, 
	
childcare and healthcare 
•	 Connecting new arrivals with services that improve their 
	
ability to live independently, like job training, English classes, 
	
education, and apprenticeships 
•	 Guiding new arrivals through the process of applying for 
	
financial support, medical help, child benefits, and other 
	
services they might need 
•	 Holding meetings in local areas and using community 
	
development principles to help those who attend 
•	 Supporting people if they face racism or other unfair 
	
treatment, helping them report it to the right authorities 
•	 Helping vulnerable new arrivals get in touch with non- 
	
governmental organisations (NGOs) and other services if 
	
they need extra help

SEAI Publish Emissions and Energy Target Progress 
for 2024 
Clare County Council is subject to two emissions reduction tar-
gets, with the first to reduce emissions by 51% from transport 
and heating and the second to reduce emissions by 51% from 
transport, heating and electricity combined consumption. SEAI 
have finalised energy reporting for the year 2024 highlighting 
Clare County Councils progress towards these targets. In 2024 
emissions from transport and heating were 17.2% below the 
baseline. To achieve our target we must reduce emissions by 
another 40.8% within the next 6 years. In 2024 emissions from 
transport, heating and electricity combined were 35.4% below 
the baseline. To achieve our target we must reduce total emis-
sions by another 53.3% within the next 6 years. 
Clare County Council is actively using HVO, a sustainable zero-
emission fuel, across our fleet and advancing the procurement 
of Electric Vehicles. We are also retrofitting large buildings 
swapping out fossil fuel heating systems for renewable sources 
such as heat pumps and biomass. We are also actively reducing 
our energy consumption through careful energy management, 
installation of energy efficient technologies such as LED lighting 
and generating our own renewable energy through the installa-
tion of Solar PV systems.
